beats.narration: Four thousand weeks. That is the entire thing — every morning you will ever wake up, every person you will ever love, all of it, in four thousand weeks.
beats.understand: the whole life, stated as one small number

beats.narration: About seventy-seven years, if you are lucky. It sounds enormous. So let's spend it, honestly, and see what is actually left at the end.
beats.understand: a real pair of old hands — the number made physical

beats.narration: Chapter one. Asleep.
beats.understand: Asleep

beats.narration: Twenty-six years of it, you are unconscious. Not resting — gone. The lights go out and the years keep moving without you.
beats.understand: a figure asleep while the nights fly past — 26 years

beats.narration: It does not feel like a cost. It feels like nothing at all. That is what makes it the largest bill you will ever pay.
beats.understand: an empty dark bedroom, the bed still holding its shape

beats.narration: Roughly a third of everything you were given, spent lying down in the dark.
beats.understand: morning light arriving on an empty room — a third of a life gone

beats.narration: Chapter two. At work.
beats.understand: At Work

beats.narration: Nine more years at work. Not nine years of workdays — nine years of solid, round-the-clock time, handed over.
beats.understand: a figure hunched at a desk as the days blur — 9 years

beats.narration: The same chair. The same light. The same twenty minutes before you are allowed to leave.
beats.understand: a real desk, worn and specific

beats.narration: About eighty thousand hours, if you work a normal life. Most people cannot name what they did with them.
beats.understand: a real worker mid-task — the hours made physical

beats.narration: Chapter three. The screen.
beats.understand: The Screen

beats.narration: Eleven years looking into a screen. This is the one nobody plans for and everybody pays.
beats.understand: a figure curled around a glowing phone as the room dims — 11 years

beats.narration: It arrives in pieces small enough to feel free. Four minutes here. A queue there. A whole evening, occasionally, with nothing to show for it.
beats.understand: a real face lit only by a phone in the dark

beats.narration: Three hours a day is the average, and that is only the television. The number under that is worse.
beats.understand: a real television glowing in an empty living room

beats.narration: Chapter four. Getting there.
beats.understand: Getting There

beats.narration: A full year of your life is spent in traffic. Sitting still, facing forward, going to the place that takes the nine years.
beats.understand: a figure motionless in a car as the road crawls — 1 year

beats.narration: Twenty-seven minutes each way, on average. It is the most ordinary theft there is.
beats.understand: a real highway, packed and patient

beats.narration: Then the lines. The waiting room. The one in front of you who has questions.
beats.understand: a figure standing in a queue that never advances

beats.narration: And the hold music, which has been playing, somewhere, for your entire adult life.
beats.understand: a figure on the phone, on hold, going nowhere

beats.narration: Chapter five. The upkeep.
beats.understand: The Upkeep

beats.narration: Four and a half years on the maintenance of being alive. Dishes. Laundry. The same surfaces, wiped again.
beats.understand: a real sink, real dishes — the unglamorous truth

beats.narration: Another two and a half years simply eating. Which, to be fair, is the good part.
beats.understand: a real table mid-meal, plates and hands

beats.narration: Lay it all out end to end and the arithmetic gets uncomfortable.
beats.understand: the whole life as a grid, the spent squares filling in

beats.narration: What is left is about nine years. Nine years of awake, unclaimed, genuinely yours time, spread thin across seventy-seven.
beats.understand: the figure standing in warm light — 9 years are yours

beats.narration: Nine years is not a tragedy. It is a budget. And almost nobody knows they are holding one.
beats.understand: a real person outdoors in late light, unhurried

beats.narration: So the question was never where the time goes. The time goes exactly where you leave it. The question is what you do with the nine years nobody is asking you for.
beats.understand: the figure walking out of frame toward the light — the payoff

beats.narration: Four thousand weeks. You have already spent some of them getting here.
beats.understand: a real horizon at first light — return to the opening
